description:
crate-jmap-tasks-server/src/backend.rs:157-164:

    fn compute_task_utc_times(
        &self,
        _task: &jmap_tasks_types::Task,
        _tz_hint: Option<&str>,
    ) -> (Option<jmap_types::UTCDate>, Option<jmap_types::UTCDate>) {
        (None, None)
    }

The method is synchronous. The canonical-pattern sibling (jmap-calendars-server) defines the corresponding method as async:

    crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/backend.rs:284-293:
    fn compute_utc_times(
        &self,
        _caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
        _account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
        _event: &jmap_calendars_types::CalendarEvent,
        _tz_hint: Option<&str>,
    ) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = (Option<...>, Option<...>)> + Send {
        async { (None, None) }
    }

A real production backend has three realistic paths to tz conversion, all of which are inconvenient or wrong under a sync contract:

  1. Embed a full tzdata blob in-process (e.g. chrono-tz or jiff with bundled-tzdata).
     Works but: ~1-2 MB binary bloat per process, no live updates when the IANA db
     ships a new release.

  2. Use the OS tz database (libc tzset()-style or /etc/localtime). Sync but
     OS-dependent and not portable across containerised deployments where
     /usr/share/zoneinfo may be stripped.

  3. Query a sidecar service (tzdb-as-an-API, or a redis/kv cache backed by an
     async-loaded source). Async by nature — but currently impossible because
     the trait signature is sync.

The shape also leaks an internal assumption: \"tz conversion is a pure
function of the task + hint\". A real backend may want to consult per-account
state (\"this account has a default tz preference\", \"this user has a tz
override stored in their profile\"). The signature does not accept a CallerCtx
or account_id parameter — neither of which calendars-server omits.

Additional differences from the calendars analog:
  - calendars passes caller and account_id; tasks passes only the object + hint.
  - calendars is async; tasks is sync.
  - calendars is on the per-domain trait, returns (utcStart, utcEnd); tasks
    returns (utcStart, utcDue). Field-name choice is correct per draft-tasks-06.

The async shape was the deliberate choice in calendars; the sync shape in tasks
appears to be drift from that canonical pattern. Either the calendars decision
should be reverted (in which case file a workspace-wide bead), or tasks should
follow it. The cookie-cutter rule in workspace AGENTS.md (\"differences should
be the specific JMAP capability the crate covers, nothing else\") points to the
latter.

A 0.x-to-0.x shape change is OK; once 1.0 ships, this is locked.
title: TasksBackend::compute_task_utc_times is sync — diverges from sibling calendars (async), forces backends to embed tzdata in-process or block the runtime
